Deputy "default" finished job 01a1955e-ca2d-7ec3-890a-3e22f6dda9b1: rc 0 (ok).
Command: aida edit STORY-2243 --title aida goal advisor set / show / check / history: the operator's standing goal for the advisor, kept in AIDA so it survives a new session --description ## Why
The operator gives the advisor a standing goal (e.g. "get the open list to zero, then improve AIDA from the regroup list") by pasting `/goal …` into one Claude session. A new or rotated advisor session loses it, and other vendors (Codex) have no `/goal`. Only the advisor needs this. Implementers already have their spec as their goal, and product orders the queue. A goal on every seat would give agents a second source of priority to reconcile.

## Scope
No new top-level command: it goes under the existing `aida goal`.
- `aida goal advisor set "<text>" [--epic ID] [--spec ID] [--batch N] [--queue-empty ROLE] [--pr N]`: stores the goal in the requirements store as free text plus ordered clauses. The clauses come from the existing `aida goal` flags, and each carries its verify command. Setting a new goal replaces the active one, and the old one stays in history. Only the operator sets it (human terminal); agents, including the advisor, cannot.
- `aida goal advisor show`: text, clauses with their verify commands, who set it and when. Supports human/toon/json.
- `aida goal advisor check`: runs each clause's verify and prints met/unmet per clause. Exit 0 only when every clause is met. A free-text-only goal reports "no checkable clauses" and never claims to be met.
- `aida goal advisor history`: past goals, newest first.
- Bare `aida goal --epic …` (derive a `/goal` line) is unchanged.
- **Scope:** the stored record carries a scope key, today always the default branch. When target branches land (EPIC-74), a goal is scoped to the branch the advisor is working, with no data rewrite. No scope flag is exposed until then.
- **Surfaces:** the advisor's launch context gets a Goal section, and `aida session handoff --seat advisor --show` includes it. In the advisor seat, `aida whoami` prints `goal:` with the set goal, and the role purpose moves to `purpose:`.

## Acceptance
1. `aida goal advisor set "X" --epic EPIC-612 --queue-empty implementer`, then `aida goal advisor show`, prints X, both clauses with verify commands, setter and timestamp, in human, toon and json.
2. The goal is canonical in the store: a fresh session and a second clone after sync show the same goal.
3. A newly launched advisor's context file contains the goal, and `aida whoami` there prints it on `goal:` (purpose on `purpose:`). Other seats' launch context and whoami do not show it.
4. `check` exits 0 with all clauses met and non-zero naming each unmet clause (fixture: one met, one unmet). A free-text-only goal reports "no checkable clauses" and exits non-zero.
5. A second `set` replaces the first, and `history` lists both, newest first.
6. `set` from a non-TTY agent session is refused with a message saying the operator sets it. `show`, `check` and `history` work from any seat.
7. The record has a scope field equal to the default branch. A unit test pins the field so EPIC-74 can key on it.
8. Regression: `aida goal --epic EPIC-612 --invoke` output is unchanged.
9. Vendor-neutral: works from a Codex seat (nothing depends on Claude `/goal`).

## Out of scope
Goals for other seats; a scope flag before EPIC-74; anything that reorders the queue. --tags goal,advisor,vendor:codex
Output: /home/joe/ai/aida/.aida/deputy/default/out/01a1955e-ca2d-7ec3-890a-3e22f6dda9b1.out
Read it with `aida deputy log 01a1955e-ca2d-7ec3-890a-3e22f6dda9b1`.
